headline: BLACKROCK-BACKED GLADIATOR DRILLS 32m AT 2.12% CU AT CUB EAST — Whitehorse Belt Extends 300m+; Program Expands to 50,000m (TSXV: GLAD)
snippet: Gladiator Metals Corp. (TSXV: GLAD) released July 22 assay results from Cub East confirming high-grade copper-gold continuity across multiple drill holes in the historical Whitehorse Copper Belt in Yukon, with best hole BCG-035 cutting 32.0 metres grading 1.36% copper and 0.63 g/t gold from 178 metres depth — including 18.0 metres at 2.12% Cu and 1.06 g/t Au — while step-out drilling has extended high-grade strike to over 300 metres. The announcement follows a $35 million investment by asset manager BlackRock last month that funded the expansion of Gladiator's 2026 Whitehorse Copper drill program from 35,000 metres to more than 50,000 metres, signalling institutional conviction that the district hosts far more mineralization than the historic record suggests.

headline: TALAMORE HITS 9.28 g/t Au AT COFFEE GOLD SUPREMO EXTENSION — 42m AT 1.50 g/t in 40k-Meter DFS Push; $130M Equity Behind This Yukon Play (TSXV: TALA)
snippet: Talamore Mining Corp. (TSXV: TALA) announced July 22 initial high-grade drill results from the Supremo Extension at its wholly-owned Coffee Gold project in Yukon Territory, with hole 26-SPX-RC084 returning 5.37 g/t Au over 8.4 metres and hole 26-SPX-RC100 cutting 1.50 g/t Au over 42.4 metres, with assays topping 9.28 g/t Au in the best individual interval, all within a zone currently hosting an Inferred Resource of 6,059 kt at 1.72 g/t Au for 335,000 oz — significantly higher than the overall 1.15 g/t Coffee project grade and representing a compelling conversion target for the Feasibility Study underway. The results come after Talamore completed a $130 million equity offering to fund an aggressive 40,000-metre 2026 infill and expansion program at Coffee Gold.

headline: SILVER SURRENDERS $60 BREAKOUT — Falls to $58.77 as Brent Hits $97 on Houthi Tanker Strikes; Oil-Driven Inflation Kills Sixth-Deficit-Year Bid
snippet: Silver fell 1.59% to $58.77 per ounce on July 23 — surrendering the brief $60–$61 test achieved after Wednesday's soft jobs data — as Brent crude surged past $97 per barrel after Iran-backed Houthi militants targeted Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, reviving inflation-premium selling that has consistently capped precious metals during the 2026 Iran conflict. Gold dropped 0.99% to $4,089 on the same session, with both metals declining even as the US dollar index fell below 101, underscoring how oil-driven inflation expectations have temporarily disconnected the safe-haven bid from geopolitical risk — a dynamic that leaves silver's sixth consecutive annual deficit of 46.3 million ounces structurally intact but overshadowed by rate-hike pricing into the July 28–29 FOMC meeting.

headline: BRIXTON DRILLS 5,015 g/t Ag OVER 20m AT NEW LANGIS ZONE — 89,125 g/t BONANZA CORE; Among Highest Silver Intercepts Globally, 100m+ Open (TSXV: BBB)
snippet: Brixton Metals Corporation (TSX-V: BBB) reported July 21 the discovery of ultra-high-grade silver in an entirely new brownfields area called Shaft 6 Southeast at its Langis Silver Project in Ontario, with hole LM-26-377 returning 20.00 metres grading 5,015 g/t silver — including a 0.65-metre bonanza interval at 89,125 g/t Ag — in a zone that has no historic underground workings and has never previously been mined. Brixton described the intercept as among the highest silver drill results reported globally, with the S6-SE zone now outlined over at least 100 metres of strike and remaining open along strike, down-plunge, and laterally — adding a third high-grade silver locus to the Langis project at a time when silver's structural supply deficit and the $58–$61 price range are attracting renewed attention from junior mining investors.

headline: NEXMETALS CUTS 11.15m AT 7.65% CuEq IN BOTSWANA — Cu-Ni Selebi Massive Sulphide Trend Reaches 1km; NASDAQ-Dual-Listed Junior (TSXV/NASDAQ: NEXM)
snippet: NexMetals Mining Corp. (TSXV/NASDAQ: NEXM) released July 22 assay results from its 30,000-metre surface drilling program at Selebi Main in Botswana, with drill hole SMD-26-212-W1 intersecting 11.15 metres of massive sulphides grading 7.65% CuEq (3.10% Cu, 2.21% Ni) — closely replicating hole SMD-25-205 (11.05m at 7.31% CuEq) and correlating with the historic hole sd119 (26.1m at 8.29% CuEq) — validating a data-driven exploration model and defining a kilometre-scale Flexure Zone trend that remains open and beyond the limits of the 2024 Mineral Resource Estimate. NexMetals is one of few TSXV juniors with a concurrent NASDAQ listing and an $80 million financing secured in 2026, positioning the company to fast-track the Botswana copper-nickel assets toward a resource expansion and updated MRE.

headline: SILVER47 DEFINES 2.74 Moz AgEq TAILINGS AT SURFACE IN TONOPAH NEVADA — 44 g/t Ag Confirmed Across Full Impoundment; Private Land, Near-Highway (TSXV: AGA)
snippet: Silver47 Exploration Corp. (TSXV: AGA) confirmed July 21 an Inferred Mineral Resource of 1.8 Moz silver and 11 koz gold (totalling 2.74 Moz silver equivalent at 68 g/t AgEq) within a surface tailings deposit at the historic Belmont mine at its Hughes Project in Tonopah, Nevada — with all 21 auger holes returning silver-gold mineralization continuously from surface to the base of the tailings over an average 3.3-metre thickness. The fine-grained Belmont tailings sit on patented claims across 84 acres of private land immediately adjacent to US Highway 6, making the near-surface resource highly amenable to low-disturbance heap-leach extraction — a particularly compelling development given Nevada permitting precedents and the current silver price environment approaching $60 per ounce.

headline: COEUR DOUBLES MEXICO EXPLORATION TO $158M — 16.5 g/t Au, 206 g/t Ag AT PALMAREJO; Las Chispas Vein Grows to 1km in Biggest-Ever Program (NYSE: CDE)
snippet: Coeur Mining (NYSE: CDE) announced July 21 a record $158 million exploration investment in its two Mexico operations — double the prior year — including $27 million at Palmarejo where hole VIDH-221 at Independencia Sur returned 9.1 metres grading 16.5 g/t gold and 206 g/t silver from 473 metres depth, and $24 million at Las Chispas where the Augusta Gap Zone has expanded multiple key veins to more than one kilometre in strike length. The scale of investment — 200,000 metres of scout, expansion, and infill drilling across both assets — signals high management conviction in resource growth potential at established Mexican producing mines, with the announcement delivering a bullish catalyst for Coeur shares and underscoring the exploration premium the current gold-silver price environment is unlocking for operators with permitted, producing platforms.

headline: KLONDIKE GOLD COMPLETES PHASE 1 DAWSON DISTRICT DRILL — 176 Oz Placer Royalty Flows From Montana Creek; Phase 2 Follows at Lone Star Zone (TSXV: KG)
snippet: Klondike Gold Corp. (TSXV: KG) announced July 23 the completion of Phase 1 of its 2026 diamond drill program targeting resource expansion at the Lone Star and Stander Zones of its 100%-owned Klondike District project in the Dawson Mining District, Yukon — one of the most storied gold camps in North America — with a second drill phase planned to follow immediately. The company simultaneously disclosed that its Montana Creek Placer royalty from Armstrong Mining Corp. has delivered a cumulative 176.1 ounces of placer flake gold as of July 20, 2026, including 136.2 ounces received since the June 1 update, demonstrating that the royalty structure is actively generating gold receipts during the current Yukon placer season.

headline: GOLD:SILVER RATIO AT 70:1 VS 56-YEAR MEAN OF 60:1 — New Study Says Silver Is Structurally Cheap; Mean Reversion Alone Implies 15% Outperformance
snippet: A research analysis released July 22 via GlobeNewswire examining January 1970 through May 2026 data argues that the gold-silver ratio retains strong predictive relevance in the modern era despite silver's expanded industrial demand profile, with the absolute long-run mean-reverting equilibrium sitting at just under 60:1 — compared to the current ratio of approximately 70:1 that reflects silver's sharper pullback from 2026 highs. The study concludes that the current spread implies meaningful structural undervaluation for silver relative to gold, with passive mean reversion to the historical equilibrium alone representing a roughly 15% outperformance for silver versus gold even with no change in the gold price — a thesis reinforced by the Silver Institute's sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces.

headline: FOMC HOLD + ETF BID ARE SILVER'S TWO CATALYSTS — Structural Deficit Already Priced In; $65 Path Opens If Rate Risk Fades July 29
snippet: GoldSilver.com's July 2026 silver price outlook identifies two specific catalysts required to unlock the next leg higher for silver beyond the $60 resistance level: a dovish or neutral Federal Reserve statement at the July 28–29 FOMC meeting confirming rate-hike risk is off the table, and a reactivation of ETF inflows that have remained subdued despite the sixth consecutive annual silver supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces. The analysis argues that the structural deficit is already known by the market and priced into physical premiums, but that ETF investors — who sit on the sidelines during periods of elevated rate uncertainty — represent the marginal buyer capable of pushing silver through $65 and on toward the $70–$80 range that would reflect the metal's historical ratio relationship with gold in a sustained precious metals bull cycle.
